messages:
maria (support): Hey team — OmniPay is stuck after upgrading to our Go SDK tagged v2.0.0. They get a go.mod parsing error. attaching logs + repro steps.

john_omni (customer): repro steps i used:
1) create new module
2) go get github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk@v2.0.0
3) go build

error: 
```
go: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk v2.0.0: parsing go.mod:
	module declares its path as: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/v2
		but was required as: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk
```

maria (support): Their project doesn't import "/v2" suffix anywhere. They have a replace pointing at a local checkout too. here's their go.mod (redacted):

```
module github.com/omnipay/processor

go 1.20

require (
    github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk v2.0.0
)

replace github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk => ../redwood-go-sdk
```

sam (go-sdk-owner): that error means the released module's go.mod uses a module path with /v2 but callers are requiring the old path. two usual fixes: change imports to use /v2 path + require v2 module, or publish a v2 tag that uses the non-/v2 module path (not recommended).

sam (go-sdk-owner): quick checks: i just looked at the v2.0.0 tag — our published go.mod indeed has `module github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/v2`. so the release assumes consumers use the v2 module import path.

alex (eng-runtime): is this a packaging mistake or did we forget to update the release notes? we should notify release folks.

maria (support): OmniPay says they upgraded the import line by only changing the tag used in go get, not the import statements. they expected a breaking change but thought go get would handle it.

sam (go-sdk-owner): right — with semantic import versioning in Go, v2+ requires the /vN suffix in module path and all imports. Workarounds for them:
- change imports from `github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk` to `github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/v2` and `go get github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/v2@v2.0.0`
- OR (temporary) add a local replace pointing to a fork that exposes the old module path (not ideal)

sam (go-sdk-owner): I'll prepare a short support note + CLI snippet.

ci-bot: Release artifact for v2.0.0 uploaded: https://ci.internal/releases/redwood-go-sdk/v2.0.0 :package:

sam (go-sdk-owner): support note snippet:
```
# Fix for consumers upgrading to v2
# 1) Update import statements in your code:
import "github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/v2"

# 2) Update your go.mod require:
require github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/v2 v2.0.0

# 3) Tidy/get:
go get github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/v2@v2.0.0
go mod tidy
```

john_omni (customer): ok i'll try updating imports. any chance we can avoid touching every file? we have many internal packages importing the old path.

maria (support): you can do a project-wide find/replace, or add a transitional module/fork as a temporary shim until you finish the refactor. i can escalate if you hit failures.

alex (eng-runtime): long-term: we should add a release checklist item to call out major-version module path changes and include an automated compatibility note in the changelog. also maybe a tool that scans our go.mod -> release tag parity.

sam (go-sdk-owner): agreed. i'll push a patch to the release playbook and create an internal issue to add a CI check that ensures the module path and semver tag are consistent.

maria (support): john, can you confirm after you try the import updates? if still broken share the output of `go env` + `go mod graph` and the exact error.

john_omni (customer): updated imports + ran `go get github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/v2@v2.0.0` — builds now, thanks! :tada:

maria (support): awesome, marking as resolved. sam will follow up on the release process changes.

sam (go-sdk-owner): follow-up issue: https://tracker.internal/RED-5823 — add CI check + update release notes template.

alex (eng-runtime): adding a quick script suggestion for support to run on customer projects to detect mismatches:
```
# quick checker
if grep -R "github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/v2" .; then
  echo "Found v2 imports"
else
  echo "No v2 imports found — consumer likely needs to migrate or use a shim"
fi
```

maria (support): thanks everyone. closing thread in support channel.
